title: GPU objects: the resource-manager tree, handles and classes
summary: Every GPU resource is an object in the resource manager's tree, created with NV_ESC_RM_ALLOC (root client, parent, new handle, class). Drake's client builds root client, device, subdevice, usermode page, address space, buffers, channel group, context share, GPFIFO channel and finally the Blackwell compute object. Freeing a parent frees its subtree. I can run his Omega model of that order, which refuses a wrong parent and a use after free.
goal: Know the RM object tree a GPU program builds before it can launch, and why the order is fixed.
key_steps: Allocate the root client; every other object hangs off it.
Create device and subdevice, then the address space and memory.
Create the channel group, context share and GPFIFO channel.
Create the compute object under the channel.
Free in reverse; a freed parent takes its whole subtree.

example.code:
note A model of the resource-manager (RM) object tree CUDApp's nvrm.c builds.
note Input on stdin, decimal triples:  3 child parent  = an allowed (child class, parent class) pair,
note 1 class parent# = allocate (parent# 0 only for the root client), 2 obj# 0 = free a subtree,
note 4 0 0 = print the live tree, 0 0 0 = end (prints the tree once more).
note Exit 0 every step accepted, 3 bad input, 6 a step refused (the model stops there).
om2
global ob uchar 4096
global on ulong 1
global inb uchar 4096
global inn ulong 1
global inp ulong 1
text hx "0123456789abcdef"
fn putc c uchar to void
put ob get on 0 c
put on 0 add get on 0 1
end
fn puts s view uchar * to void
for i ulong len s
putc get s i
end
end
fn putdec v ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
n = ulong 0
x = v
while true bound 21
put d n uchar add rem x 10 48
n = add n 1
x = div x 10
if eq x 0
break
end
end
while gt n 0 bound 21
n = sub n 1
putc get d n
end
end
fn puthex v ulong w ulong to void
putc 48
putc 120
for i ulong w
s = mul sub sub w 1 i 4
putc get hx and shr v s 0xf
end
end
fn flush to void
w = write 1 ob 0 get on 0
put on 0 0
end
note Read all of stdin; every pass adds at least one byte to a 4096-byte buffer.
fn slurp to bool
while lt get inn 0 4096 bound 4097
k = read 0 inb get inn 0 sub 4096 get inn 0
if lt k 0
ret false
end
if eq k 0
ret true
end
put inn 0 add get inn 0 ulong k
end
ret false
end
note Next decimal number in the input; returns 2^64-1 when none is left.
fn nextnum to ulong
v = ulong 0
seen = false
while lt get inp 0 get inn 0 bound 4097
c = get inb get inp 0
put inp 0 add get inp 0 1
if and ge c 48 le c 57
v = add mul v 10 ulong sub c 48
seen = true
else
if seen
ret v
end
end
end
if seen
ret v
end
ret 18446744073709551615
end
global ocls ulong 64
global opar ulong 64
global olive uchar 64
global ocnt ulong 1
global rch ulong 32
global rpa ulong 32
global rcnt ulong 1
text sal "alloc #"
text scl " class "
text sun " under #"
text sok ": ok\n"
text snp ": REFUSED, parent is not a live object\n"
text snr ": REFUSED, this class may not be a child of that class\n"
text sfu ": REFUSED, too many objects\n"
text sfr "free #"
text sfr2 ": REFUSED, not a live object\n"
text sfr3 ": freed "
text sfr4 " object(s), the whole subtree\n"
text stree "live tree:\n"
text sind "  "
text shash "#"
text sempty "  (empty)\n"
fn allowed c ulong p ulong to bool
for k ulong get rcnt 0
if and eq get rch k c eq get rpa k p
ret true
end
end
ret false
end
fn alloc c ulong p ulong to bool
n = add get ocnt 0 1
puts sal
putdec n
puts scl
puthex c 8
puts sun
putdec p
if ge n 64
puts sfu
ret false
end
if eq p 0
note Only the very first object may be parentless, and it must be the root client.
if or ne n 1 not allowed c 0
puts snr
ret false
end
else
if gt p get ocnt 0
puts snp
ret false
end
if eq get olive p 0
puts snp
ret false
end
if not allowed c get ocls p
puts snr
ret false
end
end
put ocls n c
put opar n p
put olive n 1
put ocnt 0 n
puts sok
ret true
end
note Children always have larger numbers than their parent, so one ascending pass frees a subtree.
fn free1 i ulong to bool
puts sfr
putdec i
if or eq i 0 gt i get ocnt 0
puts sfr2
ret false
end
if eq get olive i 0
puts sfr2
ret false
end
put olive i 0
n = ulong 1
for k ulong get ocnt 0
j = add k 1
if and gt j i eq get olive j 1
if eq get olive get opar j 0
put olive j 0
n = add n 1
end
end
end
puts sfr3
putdec n
puts sfr4
ret true
end
fn show i ulong d ulong to void
for k ulong d
puts sind
end
puts shash
putdec i
putc 32
puthex get ocls i 8
putc 10
for k ulong get ocnt 0
j = add k 1
if and eq get opar j i eq get olive j 1
show j add d 1
end
end
end
fn tree to void
puts stree
any = false
for k ulong get ocnt 0
j = add k 1
if and eq get olive j 1 eq get opar j 0
show j 1
any = true
end
end
if not any
puts sempty
end
end
fn main to int
if not slurp
ret 3
end
while true bound 200
op = nextnum
a = nextnum
b = nextnum
if eq op 0
tree
flush
ret 0
end
if eq op 3
if ge get rcnt 0 32
ret 3
end
put rch get rcnt 0 a
put rpa get rcnt 0 b
put rcnt 0 add get rcnt 0 1
else
ok = true
if eq op 1
ok = alloc a b
else
if eq op 2
ok = free1 a
else
if eq op 4
tree
else
ret 3
end
end
end
if not ok
flush
ret 6
end
end
end
ret 3
end

common_mistake: Retrying or reusing handles after a half-failed allocation or free. Free what exists in reverse order and stop using a handle whose state is unknown; CUDApp quarantines instead of reusing.

links.title: The driver client, call by call

evidence_note: EXERCISED as a host model only: objtree.om replays nvrm.c's allocation order with class numbers from the headers and refuses two bad sequences (exit 6). It encodes CUDApp's call sites, not the RM's full rules, and makes no ioctl. Native qualification at the pin is NOT_RUN.
